title: Ross Jenkins on Upwork: 8 account-ban risks and how to protect your freelance business
summary: Ross Jenkins, founder of DigitalME, lists eight behaviors that get freelancers banned on Upwork, such as off-platform chats and billing, fake reviews, and padded hours. The practical takeaway for running a freelance or agency business is to protect your platform account, keep payment protection, and build reputation through real client work.

principles.text: Keep client chats and billing on the platform until a contract starts; it protects you from scams and gives you recourse.
principles.quote: By only chatting with prospective clients through Upwork Messages—and this includes starting a Zoom or phone call through the platform—you can get help from Upwork if you feel that someone’s attempting to run a scam or take advantage of you.

principles.text: Escrow and hourly payment protection are why on-platform billing is safer than invoicing clients directly.
principles.quote: If it’s a fixed price contract, the client pays for the first milestone in advance. Upwork holds this money in escrow for you, meaning it’s secure in an account that only Upwork can touch.

principles.text: Earn reviews by doing quality work for real clients; faking or bribing for feedback risks your account and standing.
principles.quote: The best way to get good feedback on your Upwork profile is by doing high-quality work for real clients!

principles.text: Use a team or agency openly, but never pass off work you lack rights to as your own original product.
principles.quote: You can absolutely work with a team or build an agency on Upwork.

principles.text: Represent yourself with a real name and photo; trust is what lets clients hire someone they only meet online.
principles.quote: They still want to know that they’re working with a real person they can trust.

principles.text: Be transparent with clients about how you track hours, and only log time actually worked.
principles.quote: I log my hours manually and am fully transparent beforehand with clients about how I log hours, and why I prefer the method that I use.
